anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW address-select pin A0 (U2 pin 1) is tied to the +3.3V net, while A1-A5 (U2 pins 2-5 and 24) are on GND. This gives a 7-bit I2C address of 0x41, not 0x40.
anomalies.expected: The specification lists the PCA9685PW at I2C address 0x40, which requires all address pins (A0-A5) to be low. A0 should be on GND, as A1 is in this design.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The FCC master addresses the PCA9685 at 0x40 and gets no acknowledge, so the servo/PWM outputs cannot be driven.

anomalies.observed: Every VDD pin of the FCC1 STM32H753 (pins 11, 27, 50, 75, 100), plus VBAT (pin 6) and VDDA (pin 21), sits on its own unconnected net. None of them is on +3V3 or +3.3V.
anomalies.expected: All MCU VDD, VBAT and VDDA pins should be tied to the 3V3 rail, as the spec requires ('3V3 feeds both MCUs').

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: The flight computer would have no supply on its core and digital pins and would not boot.

anomalies.observed: The VDDA/VREF+ filter (R21, C28, C30) lands on FCC1 pin 13 (PH1), while the real VREF+ and VDDA pins (20, 21) are unconnected. The UART3 nets also land on FCC1 VCAP pins 48 and 73.
anomalies.expected: The analogue filter should connect to VDDA (pin 21) and VREF+ (pin 20). VCAP pins should only go to the regulator capacitors, and UART3 should use dedicated UART pins.
anomalies.impact: ADC reference and analogue supply are mis-routed, and UART3 is shorted to core-regulator pins, so the MCU's analogue and serial functions would not work.

parsed.summary: The most concrete deviation is the PCA9685PW address pin A0 tied to +3.3V, which moves its I2C address from the specified 0x40 to 0x41 and would stop the servo driver responding. The FCC1 supply and analogue pin mis-routing are lower-confidence observations of the same netlist.
